note: Ceilings on how often each degradation path may fire. Measured, never chosen. A budget may only be TIGHTENED — loosening one is a decision that must be argued for here, not edited quietly. See tests/test-degradation-budgets.js.
workload: first 120 clean open-sheet corpus games, scored as fit_policy scores them

fit_policy.decisionsUnreadable.what: decisions discarded because the CLICK could not be read — unmatched, ambiguous, trivial, no sheet, no user. Successor to decisionsDropped, and NOT the same quantity: coerced actions are excluded, because an Encored move or a dragged-in body was never a click and counting it as a dropped one conflated 'we could not read the label' with 'there was no label'.
fit_policy.decisionsUnreadable.granularity: 241,927 actions, so one action is 0.00041%. The ceiling sits 0.0058 points above the measurement — about 14 actions of headroom. Four decimal places is the finest cut that is not noise at this corpus size.

fit_policy.coercedActions.what: recorded actions the protocol shows were NOT clicks — Encore overrode the choice (1,116) or a phazing move dragged the mon in (220). Removed from the labeled set rather than fitted with a fabricated label. This counter is the one that had no ceiling because until 3.42.0 these turns were silently trained on.
fit_policy.coercedActions.granularity: one action is 0.00041%; the ceiling is 0.0004 points above the measurement, roughly 9 actions. A rise here means the corpus is getting more coercive, not that the fit got worse.

fit_joint.turnsUnreadable.what: joint turns the pair fit could not use because a CLICK could not be read. Successor to turnsDropped. THIS IS THE CEILING WILL WAS ASKED TO RULE ON — the old one read 5.4929% against a 5.49% limit and was red by 0.0029 points. It is not resolved by moving the line: docs/CLICK-CENSORING-FIX.md ruled the question SUPERSEDED because Stages B-C changed what 'dropped' MEANS, so the budget is re-derived here from the new counter with its granularity stated rather than re-cut against the old one.
fit_joint.turnsUnreadable.granularity: 101,459 turns, so one turn is 0.00099% — a ceiling quoted to four places can be crossed by a single turn, which is exactly how the old one went red. 0.0550 leaves 0.0071 points, about 72 turns, which is wider than the run-to-run movement of the corpus and narrow enough that a real regression still trips it.

fit_joint.coercedTurns.what: joint turns voided because at least one of the two recorded actions was not a click. Currently ZERO, and that is a fact about the joint fit rather than about the game: the joint artifact carries no `coerced` key, so this reads 0 by absence. If the joint fitter starts reporting coercion this ceiling must be re-derived, and a zero here should be read as 'not yet counted', not as 'does not happen'.
fit_joint.coercedTurns.granularity: a hard zero is only defensible while the counter is structurally absent; the moment it is populated this entry is wrong and the test will say so.

board.dmgMon.unknownSpecies.what: candidate scorings where the damage engine could not identify a Pokemon, so every damage-derived feature silently read zero

board.dmgMon.engineUnavailable.what: candidate scorings with no damage engine at all

sheet.speciesUnresolvable.what: Pokemon on real open team sheets that mcKey cannot resolve to a damage-engine entry

fit_policy.unmatchedClicks.what: human clicks the move fit could not match to a candidate, so the decision was dropped from training

fit_policy.decisionsDropped.what: decisions discarded for any reason before fitting

fit_joint.turnsDropped.what: joint turns the pair fit could not use — the defect that had it fitting 74 weights on 30% of the data

chomp_ev.unbuildableGames.what: human games CHOMP could not build a board for, so they left the evaluation set
